newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* Despite the debt of its parent company, Time Warner, Time Inc is flourishing and expects to earn more than $530 million in operating income for 1996 on more than $4 billion in revenue.

* Trade negotiators attending the World Trade Organisation are close to reaching a pact to open up government protected telecommunications monopolies, but the United States threatens to block an agreement if its demands are not met.
* China and the United States reached a broad agreement that could boost the billion-dollar textile trade between both countries.
* Mercury Finance is struggling to avoid bankruptcy after disclosing that its earnings for the past four years were overstated.
* Advertising agency Fallon McElligott is ending its relationship with McDonald's, and Chicago's Leap Partnership, the advertising unit of Leap Group, is planning an expansion into Los Angeles.
* The job market for cable installers is booming as the number and complexity of computer networks increase.

* A number of companies are moving to fill the gap between top-dollar and less costly video conferencing equipment, including Sony Corp, which plans to introduce a $7,000 system this week at a communications conference in Washington, D.C.
* Baltimore businessman Steve Geppi is moving to make Diamond Comic Distributor Inc a leading company in the comic book business by consolidating distribution.
* Los Angeles radio station KSCA-FM will switch to a Spanish-language format and will be managed by a company controlled by Clear Channel Communications Inc this week.
* America Online's flat-rate pricing strategy has put greater pressure on Internet content providers who have seen traffic at their sites double but their usage fees capped by flat-pricing.
